predecessors.name: Hongshan culture
predecessors.text: the West Liao basin, 'an area stretching from Inner Mongolia to Liaoning', where the Hongshan 'c.

successors.name: Lower Xiajiadian Culture
successors.text: the Lower Xiajiadian culture (2200-1600 BC), 'found mainly in southeastern Inner Mongolia, northern Hebei, and western Liaoning'; 'preceded by the Hongshan culture, through the transitional Xiaoheyan…

ledger.x: 3000 BCE: the Xiaoheyan culture appears at Aohan in the Hongshan country.
3000 BCE: the early Xiaoheyan distribution across Yanshan is drawn from the culture's start.
2900 BCE: the Xiaoheyan takes the Hongshan's West Liao basin.
2600 BCE: the Longshan replaces the Xiaoheyan south of Yanshan.
2000 BCE: the Xiaoheyan gives way to the Lower Xiajiadian.

certainty.note: A prehistoric culture known from sites; the page gives no frontier, only town names (Zhangjiakou, Datong, Shijiazhuang) for its early extent.
